title: CFG overshoot, measured on real renders

questions.q: In our cfg 7 against cfg 14 renders, what happened to the edge figure?
questions.why: The stored figures are 13.92 and 12.34. 30.99 is the difference from the cfg 7 picture.

questions.q: Why can raising cfg change the composition, not only the contrast?
options: The sum applies from the first step, when the broad layout is decided
questions.answer: The sum applies from the first step, when the broad layout is decided
questions.why: The early high-noise steps get the stronger push too, so the path differs from there on.

questions.q: Your picture is fried at cfg 12. What should you try first?
options: Lower cfg, keeping the seed fixed
Change the seed and keep cfg
questions.answer: Lower cfg, keeping the seed fixed
questions.why: Steps don't change the sum, and a new seed hides what cfg did. Lowering cfg removes the push itself.

questions.q: In the lab, what happens to the number of calls between cfg 2 and cfg 20?
options: It doubles every step of cfg
questions.why: Cfg above 1 costs two predictions per step, whatever its size.

questions.q: How much should you trust the wipe in this lesson as a general rule?
options: It is one seed on one model: an example of the kinds of change, not a law
It holds for every seed on SDXL
questions.answer: It is one seed on one model: an example of the kinds of change, not a law
questions.why: One render pair can't support a general claim.
